skill.name: ppt-orchestra-skill
skill.description: Plan and orchestrate multi-slide PowerPoint decks from scratch with slide type classification, layout variety, typography rules, compilation guidance, and text-based QA.
skill.summary: Plan consistent, visually varied PowerPoint decks with clear slide roles and required QA checks.
skill.author: MiniMax-AI

security_audit.summary: The skill contains no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent. Most static findings are markdown formatting false positives, but the instructions do include generated JavaScript execution and unpinned dependency installation. Review should focus on sandboxing the PPTX build step and reducing package supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: Generated slide modules are dynamically required and then executed by the Node compiler.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit manifest of expected slide files, validate file names, and run compilation in an isolated workspace.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation is unpinned and the npm command installs globally.
remediation.suggestion: Pin known safe package versions and prefer project-local npm installation over global installation.

remediation.issue: Shell commands are shown without clear execution boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands should run only in the generated slides directory on trusted presentation files.

static_findings.snippet: - **Don't forget text box padding** — when aligning lines or shapes with text edges, set `margin: 0`

- **Don't create text-only slides** — add images, icons, charts, or visual elements; avoid plain tit
- **Don't use low-contrast elements** — icons AND text need strong contrast against the background;

content.value_statement: Full decks often drift in layout, typography, and quality when slides are generated separately. This skill gives AI agents a repeatable plan for slide types, styling, compilation, and QA.
actual_capabilities: Classifies every slide into a standard deck page type.
Recommends layout patterns for text, media, data, comparisons, and timelines.
Defines typography, spacing, color, and contrast rules for consistent slides.
Provides a JavaScript compilation pattern for pptxgenjs slide modules.
Requires text extraction QA to find missing content and placeholder text.
Guides a fix-and-verify loop before the deck is considered complete.
limitations: It is an orchestration guide, not a standalone PowerPoint generator.
It assumes pptxgenjs and markitdown are available in the working environment.
It does not provide finished slide assets, templates, or brand guidelines.
It does not validate visual rendering beyond text-based QA instructions.

use_cases.title: Client Proposal Decks
use_cases.description: Plan a proposal deck with clear sections, varied layouts, and a structured final QA pass.

use_cases.title: Product Update Presentations
use_cases.description: Organize roadmap, data, comparison, and closing slides into a consistent executive presentation.

use_cases.title: Training and Workshop Materials
use_cases.description: Create educational decks with section dividers, process slides, examples, summaries, and readable typography.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 10-slide PowerPoint plan for this topic. Classify each slide type and suggest one layout for each slide.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Slide Variety
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this slide outline for repeated layouts. Revise it so content pages use varied text, media, data, comparison, and process formats.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare PPTX Generation
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this approved outline into a slide-by-slide build plan. Include page type, content blocks, typography rules, spacing, and QA checks.

prompt_templates.title: Run Full Deck QA
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this generated deck text. Identify missing content, wrong order, placeholders, weak slide variety, and fixes that need re-verification.

output_examples.input: A founder needs a concise fundraising deck for a seed-stage analytics product.
output_examples.output: A structured deck plan with cover, market problem, product, traction, business model, roadmap, team, ask, and closing slides.

output_examples.input: A product manager has 12 slide titles but many slides look similar.
output: Several slides are reassigned to comparison, timeline, data visualization, and image showcase formats.
Typography and spacing rules are applied across the full deck.

output_examples.input: A generated presentation needs final review before delivery.
output_examples.output: A QA checklist highlights missing text, placeholder content, slide order issues, and specific slides that need another verification pass.

best_practices: Classify every slide before generating slide content.
Use one consistent typography and spacing system across the deck.
Run text extraction QA and fix all issues before final delivery.
anti_patterns: Do not generate many text-only slides with the same layout.
Do not skip verification because the first render looks complete.
Do not run generated JavaScript outside a controlled working directory.

faq.question: Does this skill create a PowerPoint file by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides an AI agent through planning, slide generation, compilation, and QA.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What kind of decks work best?
faq.answer: It is best for multi-slide decks that need structure, visual variety, and consistent formatting.

faq.question: Does it require external packages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill references pptxgenjs for creation and markitdown for text extraction QA.

faq.question: Can it use company brand rules?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide fonts, colors, logo rules, and forbidden styles before slide planning starts.

faq.question: What should users review before running commands?
faq.answer: Users should review generated JavaScript files and run commands only in a controlled project folder.
